content: In these cases every genuine engine (excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula, ironcalc, lattice, and pycel where present) agrees on the numeric or error result; the only branch that diverges is libreoffice, which records a blank cell ([[null]]) for every case. The libreoffice fixtures for the math, operator, and parser suites are uniformly blank — all 65 math, 115 operator, and 34 parser results are [[null]] — which is inconsistent with genuine LibreOffice evaluation (LibreOffice computes ABS, ROUND, MOD, etc. natively). This is a recording-harness gap for these suites, not a LibreOffice semantic behavior. The fork should dissolve once the libreoffice recording for these suites is regenerated.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures: fixtures/{math,operator,parser}/libreoffice.json are 100% [[null]] (65/65, 115/115, 34/34); every other engine agrees on the real result

content: Two branches diverge from the agreeing majority. (1) pycel returns #NAME? on every one of these formulas because each contains an arithmetic operator — specifically the unary minus of a negative literal (e.g. -3.4, -2.5, -1, -3, -10, and the -2 second argument of ROUND(1234,-2)). In assay's pycel integration, any formula whose source text contains an infix or unary arithmetic operator (+, -, *, /, ^) compiles to #NAME?; formulas that are pure function calls over non-negative literals or cell references evaluate correctly. Live-probe confirmation (pycel): =ABS(-3.4)=>#NAME? but =ABS(3)=>3 and =ABS(A1) with A1=-3.4 => 3.4; =0-3.4, =10-3, =10+3, =10*3, =2+3*4 all => #NAME?; the recorded arithmetic fixture shows the same (=1+1, =10/3, =2+3*4 all #NAME?). A negative value delivered through a cell reference computes fine, so this is a formula-compilation/tokenization artifact in the pycel integration, not a numeric-semantics limitation of the underlying functions. (2) libreoffice records blank per the uniform math-suite recording gap. All other engines agree on the true result.

_meta.evidence: live probe (createDriver pycel) reproduced #NAME? for every operator-bearing formula and correct results for operator-free calls; corroborated by fixtures/arithmetic/pycel.json (6/6 operator formulas => #NAME?)

content: =SUM() with zero arguments produces a five-way split. lattice and pycel treat the empty sum as 0. gsheets and hyperformula raise #N/A. formulas raises #VALUE!. ironcalc raises #ERROR!. excel and libreoffice record blank — for libreoffice this is the suite-wide recording gap, and for excel the blank most likely reflects that Excel rejects =SUM() as a malformed formula at entry (it requires at least one argument), so no value is captured rather than a computed blank. The engines disagree on whether a no-argument SUM is a syntax/arity error (and which error code to surface) or a well-defined empty aggregate equal to 0.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures partition; excel=blank interpretation is inferred (Excel rejects zero-arg SUM at entry) and flagged for probe

content: ADD is Google Sheets' function-name alias for the binary + operator; it is not part of the Excel function set. excel, formulas, hyperformula, ironcalc, and pycel therefore return #NAME? (unknown function). gsheets and lattice implement ADD, and here both return #VALUE! because the first argument "abc" is a non-numeric string that cannot coerce to a number — so the two engines that support the function agree on the coercion error. libreoffice records blank per the suite-wide recording gap. This extends the missing-function story in DV-0002 (which covers ADD's numeric tests) to the non-numeric-string argument case, where the supporting engines' error attribution (#VALUE!) becomes visible.

_meta.evidence: live probe confirmed formulas/hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel => #NAME? for =ADD("abc",1); recorded fixtures give gsheets/lattice => #VALUE!; extends DV-0002

content: GT, GTE, and LTE are Google Sheets function-name aliases for the comparison operators >, >=, <=; they are absent from the Excel function set, so excel, formulas, hyperformula, ironcalc, and pycel return #NAME? (confirmed live for formulas/hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel). The two engines that implement them, gsheets and lattice, diverge on how a boolean compares against a number: GT(TRUE,0) is TRUE in gsheets but FALSE in lattice; GTE(TRUE,1) is TRUE in gsheets but FALSE in lattice; LTE(FALSE,0) is FALSE in gsheets but TRUE in lattice. Every result is consistent with gsheets ranking booleans above all numbers (Excel/Sheets cross-type ordering number < text < boolean, so any boolean is greater than any number), whereas lattice ranks booleans below numbers (so any boolean is less than any number). Neither engine is coercing TRUE to 1 / FALSE to 0 here — a numeric coercion would make GTE(TRUE,1) true in both. libreoffice records blank per the suite-wide recording gap.

_meta.evidence: live probe confirmed the #NAME? branch (formulas/hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel); gsheets-vs-lattice ordering inferred from recorded fixtures (self-consistent boolean-rank model); needs live gsheets confirmation

content: UNIQUE is a dynamic-array (spilling) function. excel, formulas, gsheets, and lattice implement it and agree on the deduplicated spill for numeric, string, all-identical, no-duplicate, and 2D-row inputs. hyperformula, ironcalc, and pycel do not implement UNIQUE and return #NAME? (confirmed live for hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel). libreoffice records blank per the suite-wide recording gap. The split is purely support-vs-no-support; every engine that has the function produces the same result on these inputs.

_meta.evidence: live probe: hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel => #NAME?, formulas spills correctly (=UNIQUE(A1:A3){1,1,2} => [1;2]); excel/gsheets/lattice spill in recorded fixtures

content: With mixed-case duplicates (grid A1:A3 = "Apple", "apple", "APPLE") UNIQUE's case-sensitivity divides the engines that support it. excel treats the three as a single value and returns one result, "Apple" (case-insensitive deduplication, keeping the first occurrence). formulas, gsheets, and lattice treat case as significant and return all three distinct strings "Apple", "apple", "APPLE" (case-sensitive deduplication). hyperformula, ironcalc, and pycel return #NAME? (UNIQUE unimplemented). libreoffice records blank per the suite-wide recording gap. This is a genuine documented Excel-vs-Sheets difference: Excel's UNIQUE compares text case-insensitively, Google Sheets' UNIQUE is case-sensitive.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures: excel=1 result (Apple), formulas/gsheets/lattice=3 results; consistent with documented Excel case-insensitive UNIQUE; excel keep-first and gsheets both flagged for live confirmation

content: CONVERT (unit conversion) is implemented by excel, formulas, gsheets, ironcalc, and lattice but not by hyperformula or pycel, which return #NAME? (confirmed live; ironcalc computes =CONVERT(1,"m","ft") => 3.280839895 and formulas => 3.280839895013123). Among the supporting engines the answer is numerically the same conversion but the recorded precision differs: excel and formulas carry full IEEE-754 double precision (m->ft = 3.2808398950131235 / 3.280839895013123), whereas gsheets and ironcalc record a value rounded to about 9 decimal places (3.280839895). This precision-of-record variance (also seen for kg->lbm and km->mi) is why the supporting engines land in a class with several recorded value variants. libreoffice records blank per the suite-wide recording gap. Extends the CONVERT missing-function story in DV-0016 and the CONVERT precision story in DV-0206 to the meters/kilograms/kilometers cases.

_meta.evidence: live probe: hyperformula/pycel => #NAME?, ironcalc => 3.280839895, formulas => 3.280839895013123; recorded fixtures show excel full-double and gsheets 9dp; extends DV-0016 / DV-0206

content: For invalid unit requests CONVERT produces two visually-similar but mechanistically different errors. excel, formulas, gsheets, ironcalc, and lattice implement CONVERT and return #N/A when the units are incompatible (ft->kg, a length-to-mass conversion) or unknown ("xyz"): the function exists and rejects the argument. hyperformula and pycel do not implement CONVERT at all and return #NAME? (unknown function) regardless of the unit arguments (confirmed live: ironcalc =CONVERT(1,"ft","kg") => #N/A, hyperformula/pycel => #NAME?). libreoffice records blank per the suite-wide recording gap. So the #N/A branch is a domain/argument rejection by a present function, while the #NAME? branch is the absence of the function — same error surface, different cause.

_meta.evidence: live probe: ironcalc =CONVERT(1,"ft","kg") => #N/A; hyperformula/pycel => #NAME?; recorded fixtures give excel/formulas/gsheets/lattice => #N/A
